stem.text: Consider the curve given by \( \left(y + 1\right)^{2} = 2\left(- x - 1\right)^{2}\left(5 - x\right) \). The derivative is \( \frac{dy}{dx} = - \frac{6 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 1\right)}{2 y + 2} \). Find all points on the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal.

answer_key.label: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (3, 7) \) and \( (3, -9) \).

worked_solution.text: The numerator is zero where \( x = -1 \) or \( x = 3 \). At \( x = -1 \) the curve gives \( y = -1 \), where the denominator is also zero, so no horizontal tangent is decided there.
worked_solution.rule_named: numerator zero with a nonzero denominator

worked_solution.text: At \( x = 3 \) the relation gives \( \left(y + 1\right)^{2} = 64 \), so \( y = 7 \) or \( y = -9 \), and the denominator is not zero at either.
worked_solution.rule_named: solve the relation and the condition together

worked_solution.text: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (3, 7) \) and \( (3, -9) \).
